gaps: The browsed primary/authoritative materials support Shuowen’s account and a university lexicon’s reported bronze forms, but no actual glyph image was visually inspected here; detailed stroke-by-stroke development and claims of graphic corruption remain unverified.

The exact date and earliest surviving attestation of 難 as a bird name were not established. Shuowen (Eastern Han lexicographic source) records the bird gloss, while the consulted lexicon reports bronze uses for the borrowed difficulty sense but does not date or document an early bird-name occurrence in a dated inscription.

The sound/referent of the bird itself is not independently recoverable from the sources inspected. This limits claims about why the bird-name could be borrowed; the independently reported semantic and phonetic roles within the graph remain separate questions.

A competing mnemonic that 又 grasps a bird is unsupported by the inspected paleographic sources. The local update metadata calling the character ideographic with 又 and 隹 is contradicted by the external dictionary analysis and should not be used as historical evidence.

A secondary corpus excerpt proposes Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mV-nar and Tibetan/Burmese cognates, but no primary comparative-linguistic source was inspected here; the proposal and any sound-history connection therefore remain unverified and are not adopted as established character etymology.

The CUHK component analysis describes alternate accounts of the early 堇-related graph and says a sound grouping later split into distinct forms. Exact OC readings for both 堇 and 難 were not checked in the required local Baxter–Sagart table, so no Baxter–Sagart phonetic comparison is asserted.

Unicode’s official per-character Unihan pages were attempted for U+96BE and U+96E3 but were inaccessible through the browser. The supplied local kMandarin values are recorded as local rows, not claimed as externally inspected official records.

The 1935 primary document includes 难 and says the table generally selected established popular forms, but the specific claim that this form was derived from cursive 難 was not established. Its reported withdrawal in 1936 was not confirmed from a primary withdrawal notice.

The shift from the older bird-name use to difficulty, disaster, or other senses is described by the dictionary as phonetic borrowing; a complete dated sequence of early textual attestations for each sense was not obtained, so no detailed chronology is inferred.

No exact Xiaoxuetang 難 query record with its original source labels and direct glyph image URLs was available in the retrieved materials, so no image asset could be proposed under the stated image-provenance requirements.
No exact Wikimedia Commons File: description page for 難 was found; the returned files were unrelated, so none is proposed.

No physical artifact photograph or inspected glyph pixels were obtained. Chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw expressly states All Rights Reserved; its character record is cited for identity and labels only, not used as an image asset.
The earliest surviving occurrence and exact date of 難 as a bird name remain unestablished. Shuowen records the bird gloss, while the inspected lexicon reports bronze uses for borrowed senses.

The identification and pronunciation of the bird represented by the name 難/𪅀 are not independently recovered. Therefore the borrowing's original spoken form and exact sound match cannot be established from these sources.

The early 堇 component's depiction is disputed; the CUHK account reports a 火-to-variant change and discusses multiple interpretations. The traditional hand-grasping-a-bird mnemonic is unsupported by the inspected sources.
The semantic path from bird name to difficulty, disaster, question or long-lived is not demonstrated by a complete dated sequence. No chronology is inferred from a gloss list.
